stage: StoreMind Stage B structured escalation response

comparisonBar.candidateA: Official ServiceNow Retail Operations Management mechanism shown in docs/reference-materials/servicenow/2026-09-02/store-task-doc.png
comparisonBar.candidateB: Current StoreMind deterministic control-desk implementation and live browser output
comparisonBar.winnerRule: Candidate B must beat Candidate A on clarity, speed, traceability, and authorization integrity

loops.verbatimVerdict: The signed Stage A floor makes this non-negotiable: StoreMind already enforces role queue → Claim → owner-only Handoff → clock-out return_to_role, while the exact command arrays include Claim and exclude Handoff until named ownership exists. A may be one command faster for manager-pushed delegation, but importing direct Assign would change signed authorization observables and is disqualified.
loops.biggestRemainingGap: Manager-initiated push delegation remains a future-stage opportunity.

loops.verbatimVerdict: Against A's generic role-gated task/activity mechanism, B is materially clearer and faster through explicit reason/severity/trend plus high=4h and medium=8h countdown; more traceable through one active escalation and durable escalation/de-escalation history; and preserves server-derived authorization and proof-backed closure.
loops.biggestRemainingGap: Disclose that de-escalation requires justification before opening its form.

loops.verbatimVerdict: B exceeds A's optional comment attachment and role-gated manual close: proof is admitted only on verify, must match the server-issued type/artifact/source tuple, receives deterministic persisted identity, cannot be reused, and is followed by an originating-source observation that deterministically leaves work active or resolves it.
loops.biggestRemainingGap: Explicit manual reopen has no mandatory reason; this remains outside the unchanged Stage A resolution cut.

loops.verbatimVerdict: B exposes authorization-scoped store and district rollups with active, escalated, response-overdue, and oldest-response-due values; rows navigate to the scoped queue; escalation deadlines are server-authored, severity-bound, visibly active/overdue/closed, and backed by durable history. A's richer enterprise machinery is outside this cut.
loops.biggestRemainingGap: Navigation stops at a scoped queue instead of opening the exact oldest escalation.
